correctness.rationale: C PASS: Each selected reachability column is a standard basis vector, so rank equals number of covered coordinates. At each residue s modulo n, the q independent binary choices aggregate to independent Bin(q,1/2) count C_s. A coordinate s is missing exactly if C_s=q and C_(s−r)=0, with marginal probability p=4^-q. Two missing-coordinate events sharing a binomial variable conflict exactly when their residues differ by ±r; nonadjacent sets have product probability p^j. Therefore expanding z^X yields the independence polynomial of g disjoint cycles of length d=n/g, with length-two interpreted as K2. The classic cycle count d/(d−j) binom(d−j,j), quadratic-root formula and q=1 evaluation J_d(−1/4)=2^(1−d) give all exact finite laws and 2^g shortest-horizon schedules. The bounded-degree conflict graph eliminates O_k(n^(k−1)) of n^k ordered distinct k-tuples, proving uniform factorial-moment Poisson convergence when np->lambda>0; union bound handles lambda=0, variance<=np and Chebyshev handle np diverging. Independent exhaustive direct schedule enumeration vs polynomial coefficient combinatorics passed 66 cases including d=2; finite checks are corroboration not asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: O PASS qualified: cycle independence polynomial, probability generating functions, occupancy limits and factorial-moment Poisson methods are classical. The asserted new synthesis is the exact distribution of rank loss for a constrained random actuator schedule, the arithmetic gcd-dependent shortest-horizon count, and uniform critical window. Prior actuator-scheduling work treats algorithmically designed or rank-guaranteed schedules with different sampling; published general occupancy limits could subsume the convergence statement, but not the exact finite PGF without identifying this conflict graph.
residual_risks: Classical local occupancy and avoidance-pattern literature could contain an equivalent full PGF; no unconditional originality certification.

value.rationale: V PASS: Rank deficiency and full controllability probability under pointwise-sparse random actuation are natural design benchmarks. The exact all-n, all-r distribution and an offset-uniform Poisson crossover near n log_4 n give useful quantitative information beyond guaranteed feasibility; the nontrivial gcd dependence at shortest horizon is meaningful.

final_claim: For independent uniform two-choice cyclic shift actuator schedules of h=qn steps, n>=2, 1<=r<n, g=gcd(n,r), d=n/g, the exact reachability rank-deficiency PGF is J_d(4^-q(z-1))^g with cycle independence polynomial J_d. Exactly 2^g of the shortest-horizon 2^n schedules are full rank; for n->infinity, X tends to Poisson(lambda) whenever n4^-q tends to finite lambda, and full-rank probability tends to zero if n4^-q diverges, uniformly in r.
limitations: The q symbol is an integer repeat count and not a field size; do not conflate with record 1. The transition is lattice-scaled in q; time horizons not multiples of n are excluded.
